findings.claim: Removing lastClosedId satisfies the product rule that a non-Cruz-Verde offer always closes, including reappearance of a previously closed service id. The residual dedupe pendingCloseId only blocks while its 500 ms timer coroutine is running; the coroutine clears it on every terminal outcome (CLOSED, CV_RENDERED, NO_POPUP, NO_OFFER, CLICK_FAILED, exception), so no permanent blacklist can form. The remaining failure mode is a non-closing popup: retries stop after three attempts within one appearance, but every later event with Aceptar reschedules because nothing remembers prior attempts, which can produce repeated click attempts on a stuck popup until the user dismisses it or the CV node renders; those attempts are no-ops when the X is absent and are logged individually.

findings.claim: pendingCloseId is the sole guard against timer duplication for a reappearance of the same id while an earlier timer is still pending. If a new offer window for the same id appears within the 500 ms window after the timer fired and the coroutine already reset pendingCloseId, a second timer is scheduled harmlessly; if it appears before the coroutine resets it, scheduling is skipped by that event but the running coroutine still re-reads windows and closes the current popup under the service-node rule, so the close is not lost. On exception paths scheduleNonCvClose resets pendingCloseId inside the finally block, so a crash in the coroutine cannot leave a stuck guard.
